claim.supported_scope: A planned indexed nonparametric case bootstrap that fully re-estimates plsc_v2 for 1,000 through 10,000 replicates within the qualified reflective PLSc model scope and reports bounded percentile and BCa inference.
claim.estimand: The finite-sample resampling distribution, standard error, bias, and confidence interval of each canonically identified attenuation-corrected PLSc path and loading under empirical case resampling.
assumptions: The point model satisfies and successfully estimates the exact plsc_v2 reflective path-or-factor-weighting contract.
Complete cases are exchangeable sampling units and resampling rows with replacement represents the intended sampling design.
Every accepted replicate re-estimates weights, rho_A, corrected correlations, corrected loadings, structural paths, and R-squared rather than reusing the original correction.
exclusions: Studentized PLSc intervals, clustered or stratified resampling, case weights, interactions, higher-order constructs, PCA weighting, multigroup inference, and matrix-only data are excluded.
Ordinary PLS bootstrap estimates cannot substitute for full replicate-level PLSc re-estimation.
Confidence intervals do not repair misspecification, nonexchangeable observations, inadmissible PLSc solutions, or weak measurement.
warnings: Bootstrap validity remains conditional on the frozen model, sampling unit, complete-case policy, and usable-replicate threshold.
Inadmissible rho_A or corrected-correlation replicates must remain explicit failures and may not be clamped or silently replaced.

references.citation: Dijkstra and Henseler (2015), Consistent Partial Least Squares Path Modeling
Efron (1979), Bootstrap Methods: Another Look at the Jackknife
Planned independent Python full-reestimation PLSc bootstrap, percentile, and BCa implementation
Planned hand-worked indexed resample, standard-error, quantile, and identity fixture

simulations.design: Reflective common-factor models spanning path size, loading reliability, indicator count, sample size, collinearity, nonnormality, and near-inadmissible attenuation correction.
simulations.seed_policy: Scenario and replicate indexed streams independent of worker count; QuickPLS and the independent reference receive identical resample indices.
simulations.acceptance_rule: For every preregistered supported cell, empirical interval coverage must lie inside its binomial acceptance band, median bias and standard-error ratios must meet the frozen method-specific envelope, and usable replicate rate must meet the independently reviewed threshold.

simulations.design: Small-sample and weak-reliability cells that generate improper rho_A, inadmissible corrected correlations, nonconvergence, singular equations, and delete-one failures.
simulations.seed_policy: Frozen scenario-indexed streams with no retry or replacement stream.
simulations.acceptance_rule: Every attempt must be accounted for exactly, failure reasons must agree with the independent implementation, and no interval may be published when its frozen usable or jackknife requirements fail.

boundaries.case: A resample yields materially improper rho_A, a corrected correlation outside its admissible bound, nonconvergence, singularity, or nonfinite parameters.
boundaries.expected_behavior: The replicate is recorded as failed under a stable reason without clamping, retrying, or entering any parameter distribution.

boundaries.case: The recipe requests a nonreflective, interaction, higher-order, PCA-weighted, weighted, grouped, matrix-only, studentized, or out-of-range bootstrap design.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Typed validation blocks execution before creating a replicate plan.

boundaries.case: Rows and construct declarations are consistently reordered while canonical identities and seed are preserved.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Mapped resample plans and analytical summaries agree within the frozen tolerance.

boundaries.case: The same run executes under every supported worker count and scheduling order.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Resample indices, failures, ordering, summaries, and interval payloads are exactly equal.

boundaries.case: The seed, resample count, failure accounting, parameter identity, interval, PLSc version, dataset identity, or method identity is changed.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Strict project validation rejects the archive rather than displaying or exporting the changed inference.

tamper_tests.expected_behavior: Reject an inference artifact whose consistent-bootstrap capability differs from the PLSc recipe.
Reject a plsc_bootstrap_v1 artifact paired with the wrong PLSc or resampling version.
Reject a result whose complete-case dataset fingerprint or row manifest no longer matches.
Reject any changed archive member whose checksum differs.
Reject duplicate keys, unknown fields, nonfinite summaries, bad counts, identities, quantiles, intervals, or failure reasons.
Never reinterpret ordinary indexed_resampling_v1 through v4 output as consistent bootstrap evidence.

persistence.legacy_policy: Only a typed plsc_bootstrap_v1 artifact paired with exact plsc_v2 provenance may satisfy this contract.

applicability_blockers: Point PLSc model is unsupported or inadmissible
Unsupported studentized clustered weighted grouped or matrix-only request
Replicate count outside the bounded range
native.gui_cli_parity_rule: For the same recipe, seed, method versions, and dataset fingerprint, GUI and CLI resample plans and analytical payloads must be exactly equal apart from operational timestamps.
accessibility_rules: All confidence-interval graphics have equivalent accessible tables.
Failure accounting, unavailable reasons, method identity, and warnings are available without color or pointer interaction.
